result.topic_en: Euler explains that the variation of a double integral ∬V dx dy is dt∬(dV/dt)dx dy, which may be written as an iterated integral in either order, and then substitutes the variation of V from §23 to obtain a sum of double integrals involving N, P, Q, R and their primed coefficients.
result.transcription:
50 METHODVS NOVA CALCVLVM

25. Quodſi ergo huiusmodi formulae integralis $\int\int V\,dx\,dy$ variatio quaeri debeat, vbi V denotat expreſſionem quamcunque vel primi vel ſecundi generis, ex ſuperioribus ſatis liquet hanc variationem ita expreſſum iri:
$dt\int\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dx\,dy.$
quae forma iterum eſt integralis duplicata et prouti vel $x$ vel $y$ priore integratione vt conſtans ſpectatur, ea formula vel hoc modo
$dt\int dx\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dy,$
vel hoc modo
$dt\int dy\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dx$
exhiberi poteſt.

26. Sit nunc V talis expreſſio qualem ſupra § 19 deſcripſimus et cuius variationem ſeu valorem $\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)$ in § 23 euoluimus, tantum opus erit, ſingula membra ibi expoſita heic loco $\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)$ ſubſtituere; vnde ſequens congeries formularum integralium naſcetur, quibus iunctim ſumtis variatio quaeſita $dt\int\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dx\,dy$ exprimetur:
$dt\int\int N\left(\frac{dz}{dt}\right)dx\,dy+dt\int\int P\left(\frac{ddz}{dx\,dt}\right)dx.\,dy+dt\int\int Q\left(\frac{d^3z}{dx^2\,dt}\right)dx\,dy+dt\int\int R\left(\frac{d^4z}{dx^3\,dt}\right)dx\,dy$
$+dt\int\int P'\left(\frac{ddz}{dy\,dt}\right)dx\,dy+dt\int\int Q'\left(\frac{d^3z}{dx\,dy\,dt}\right)dx\,dy+dt\int\int R'\left(\frac{d^4z}{dx^2\,dy\,dt}\right)dx\,dy$
$+dt\int\int Q''\left(\frac{d^3z}{dy^2\,dt}\right)dx\,dy+dt\int\int R''\left(\frac{d^4z}{dx\,dy^2\,dt}\right)dx\,dy$
$+dt\int\int R'''\left(\frac{d^4z}{dy^3\,dt}\right)dx\,dy$
etc.

27.

items.quote:
Quodſi ergo huiusmodi formulae integralis $\int\int V\,dx\,dy$ variatio quaeri debeat, vbi V denotat expreſſionem quamcunque vel primi vel ſecundi generis, ex ſuperioribus ſatis liquet hanc variationem ita expreſſum iri:
$dt\int\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dx\,dy.$
items.english: If therefore the variation of such an integral formula ∬V dx dy is to be found, where V denotes any expression of either the first or the second kind, it is sufficiently clear from the foregoing that this variation will be expressed thus: dt∬(dV/dt) dx dy.

items.quote:
ea formula vel hoc modo
$dt\int dx\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dy,$
vel hoc modo
$dt\int dy\int\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)dx$
exhiberi poteſt.
items.english: That formula can be exhibited either in this way, dt∫dx∫(dV/dt)dy, or in this way, dt∫dy∫(dV/dt)dx.

items.quote: tantum opus erit, ſingula membra ibi expoſita heic loco $\left(\frac{dV}{dt}\right)$ ſubſtituere
items.english: It will only be necessary to substitute here, in place of (dV/dt), the individual terms set out there.
